supported_claims.text: 你 is used as a singular second-person pronoun, “you.” The dossier supports a proposed phono-semantic construction: 亻 contributes the person meaning and 尔 is proposed as the sound element. This is a source interpretation, not a directly established paleographic analysis.

The visible form has 亻 on the left and 尔 on the right. In the proposed analysis, 亻 is the semantic component. 尔 is a shortened form of 爾 in its own reported graphic history; that relationship does not itself prove 尔’s phonetic role in 你.

A competing interpretation treats 人 and 尔 as an ideographic combination, with the parts contributing “person” and “you.” The inspected evidence does not establish this analysis over the proposed phono-semantic account.

The reported account says 你 is absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and from Shuowen. It records a second-person use in 集韻 and quotes uses from historical texts. The exact earliest surviving attestation and the dating of the quoted wording are not established here.
The records also list plural, possessive, and generic uses, but do not establish their dates or how they developed from the singular pronoun. These are not enough to construct a semantic chronology.

A proposed sound comparison can be stated in modern Mandarin: 尔 ěr and 你 nǐ. These readings are supplied as current-reading metadata; they do not establish a historical sound relationship. In Baxter–Sagart’s reconstruction table, 尔 is given as Middle Chinese nyeX and Old Chinese *n[ə][r]ʔ, but no matched 你 entry was inspected in that system.

disagreements.text: The formation accounts differ: one calls 你 phono-semantic, assigning meaning to 亻 and sound to 尔; another proposes an ideographic combination of 人 and 尔. The dossier’s inspected evidence does not resolve the disagreement, and the ideographic account is not independently established.

limitations.text: No inspected paleographic source directly analyzes the formation of 你, and no verified historical glyph image for the full character is supplied. A small-seal-style image in the dossier is described as a modern font construction, not an attested historical form.
The dossier does not establish an original depicted object or an independently recoverable object-name pronunciation for 尔. Do not explain 你 as a graph borrowed from an object-name on this evidence.

The modern Mandarin pair 尔 ěr and 你 nǐ is a usable reading comparison, but it does not establish the proposed historical phonetic role. The inspected Baxter–Sagart table provides no within-system 你–尔 pair; no verified historical comparison in another single system is supplied.
The exact earliest attestation of the written graph 你 remains unresolved. Reported dictionary citations do not independently establish when the quoted passages were composed or transmitted.
No dated evidence establishes transitions among the listed plural, possessive, and generic uses. Their ordering and semantic links remain unresolved.
